label: Gratitude
title: Bhagavad Gita on Gratitude: 7 Verses to Notice What You Have
description: Seven verses on gratitude, from 'I am the taste in water' (7.8) to giving back what you've been given (3.13). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try with each.
h1: Bhagavad Gita on gratitude: 7 verses to notice what you have
subtitle: For a good day you want to remember. Read one a day, or all seven over morning tea.
intro: Krishna tells Arjuna where to look for him: in the taste of water, the light of the sun and moon, the strength in people (7.8). These verses start there, with the ordinary things we stop noticing. Then they ask what we owe back (3.12), find the spark in whatever shines (10.41), and turn gratitude into action: share first (3.13), give well (17.20). The last is from the Ramcharitmanas, a boatman who refused his fare.

days.heading: The taste in water
days.line: I am the taste in water, the light of the sun and moon, the sound in space, the strength in people.
days.forYou: Krishna could have pointed to temples or miracles. He points to water, sunlight and sound, the things you used today without a thought. Gratitude in the Gita starts with noticing them.
days.today: Drink your next glass of water slowly, and taste it.

days.heading: What you receive, you owe
days.line: Enjoy what life gives without giving anything back, and you are no better than a thief.
days.forYou: Krishna's word is stena, thief. The food, air and help that keep you going came from somewhere. Taking them as your due quietly turns a gift into a theft. Gratitude starts the giving back.
days.today: Give back one small thing today to someone or something that keeps you going.

days.heading: A spark of something larger
days.line: Whatever shines with excellence, beauty or power, see it as a spark of the divine.
days.forYou: A friend's kindness, a child's laugh, a piece of music that stops you. Krishna says each is a spark of his radiance. Seeing them that way makes the good in your day feel less like luck and more like a gift.
days.today: Name three things that shone today, however small.

days.heading: Held up by the earth
days.line: I enter the earth and hold up every living thing. As the moon's nectar, I nourish every plant.
days.forYou: The ground under you, the rain, the plants on your plate. Krishna says he is the power holding all of it up. Every meal sits on a long chain of things you didn't make.
days.today: Before your next meal, pause for a few seconds and think of where it came from.

days.heading: Share before you eat
days.line: Those who share first are freed; those who cook only for themselves feed on wrong.
days.forYou: In many Indian homes the first portion goes to the gods, the cow or a guest before the family eats. Krishna's point is simple: share first. A grateful life shows up at the table.
days.today: Share something you have today before you enjoy it yourself: food, time or a skill.

days.heading: Give the right way
days.line: Give because giving is right, to someone who can't repay you, at the right time and place.
days.forYou: Krishna's best kind of giving, sāttvika dāna, expects nothing back, goes where it's needed, and comes at the right time. That is gratitude, passed on.
days.today: Give something this week to someone who can't return the favour.

days.heading: The boatman who refused his fare

story.title: Kevat at the Ganga
story.body: Kevat, a boatman, would not take Ram across the Ganga until he had washed Ram's feet, joking that dust which once turned a stone into a woman might turn his boat into one too. Ram laughed and agreed. On the far bank Sita offered her ring as the fare. Kevat folded his hands and refused. He had worked for wages all his life, he said, and today he had been paid in full.
story.lesson: Some things can't be priced, and gratitude can be payment enough.

verse.sanskrit: नाथ आजु मैं काह न पावा । मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा ॥ बहुत काल मैं कीन्हि मजूरी । आजु दीन्ह बिधि बनि भलि भूरी ॥
verse.line: I've worked for wages all my life. Today I was paid in full.

days.forYou: Kevat counted the moment itself as his reward. Some of your best days will feel like that too.
days.today: Tell one person today, specifically, what they've given you.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about gratitude?
faq.a: Krishna asks Arjuna to see him in ordinary things: the taste of water, the light of the sun and moon (7.8). He says enjoying what we're given without giving back is theft (3.12), and that those who share before they eat are freed (3.13).

faq.q: Which Gita verse is about being thankful for food?
faq.a: 3.13 says those who eat after offering and sharing are freed from fault. 15.14 says Krishna is the fire within that digests food, which is why many families say a verse before meals.

faq.q: Is there a Gita verse about giving?
faq.a: 17.20 describes the best kind of giving: given because it's right, to someone who can't repay, at the right time and place.
